correctness.rationale: With q=4 and τ(a,b,c)=(-c,-b,-a) mod4, there are exactly eight τ-fixed triples among 64, leaving 28 nonfixed τ-orbit edges. Quotient two-letter τ-orbits give ten multigraph vertices with six odd degrees (00,01,03,12,21,22). A negative-orientable cyclic word selects pairwise distinct quotient edges in a closed walk; an Eulerian selected subgraph must omit ≥3 edges, so length≤25. Exactly 25 would omit a perfect matching among those six odd vertices. Exhaustive 28-edge quotient construction yields exactly two matchings, represented by 001/032/122 and 003/012/221. For a nonfixed pair v, the τ-invariant edge flux φ_v(a,b,c)=p_v(a,b)−p_v(b,c) telescopes to zero along any cycle. The two omission choices leave total flux −2 at v=12 and +2 at v=03 respectively, obstructing a 25-cycle. The explicitly given cyclic word 003122113232010233313033 has 24 distinct nonfixed τ-orbits. Independently recomputed all 64 triples, quotient parity, two matching choices, both fluxes and witness windows; source verifier Git blob 2c77445b35319f5b725ad8d0e73c4a637a27b1c9 uses exhaustive finite universe. value.rationale: Negative-orientable sequences are canonical cyclic position codes robust to reversal followed by additive negation. The four-symbol, length-three case is a natural explicitly published smallest open instance. Tightening the known construction and upper bounds to a provable 24-position exact maximum via combinatorial parity plus a new flux obstruction resolves a mathematically motivated finite classification, even without a general (q,n) theorem.
